source.title: Characterization of innexin gene expression and functional roles of gap-junctional communication in planarian regeneration
source.location: Table 1 (raw counts) and bar graph; Fig 10I images

injury: four transverse cuts giving head, pre-pharyngeal, trunk, post-pharyngeal and tail fragments

intervention.timing: immediately before amputation, through first 2 days
intervention.description: heptanol 0.0045-0.006% (v/v) in spring water from just before transverse amputation for 2 days, then washed into worm water

readout.method: stereomicroscope scoring of the posterior blastema regenerate of each fragment

notes: Table 1 raw counts: weak anteriorization (missing tail or bipolar pharynx) 9 + stronger anteriorization (incomplete ectopic head with eye structures) 0 coded as other; complete anteriorization (bipolar head with 2 eyes) 0 coded double_head. Scored at 14-20 days on posterior blastema of the original fragment. Dose range given as 0.0045-0.006% in methods (text also says 1-10 uM).

source.title: Characterization of innexin gene expression and functional roles of gap-junctional communication in planarian regeneration
source.location: Fig 10III legend and Results text (43%, n=423)

injury: transverse cuts anterior and posterior to the pharynx

intervention.timing: immediately before amputation, through first 2 days
intervention.description: heptanol 0.0045-0.006% (v/v) in spring water from just before transverse amputation for 2 days, then washed into worm water

readout.method: stereomicroscope scoring of the posterior blastema regenerate

notes: Legend: 43% anteriorized (18% strong: two heads and two pharynxes; 25% weak: two pharynxes but no head or cyclops head at posterior end); normal = 57% (bar). Counts converted from percentages with n=423. Text says 16% complete bipolar heads, legend says 18%; legend used. Scored at 7 days, a separate experiment from Table 1 trunk row (n=111, scored at 14-20 days); n=423 in text/legend is attributed to trunk fragments.
